name: Kendrick Lamar
label: pgLang / Top Dawg / Aftermath / Interscope
lede: A stuttering kid from Compton freestyled for two hours to get signed, then won a Pulitzer, played a Super Bowl halftime show and made a double album that opens in a therapist's chair.

eras.title: A quiet kid called K.Dot
eras.text: Compton, a stutter, a teacher who handed him poetry, and a high-school friend who drove in from Inglewood to watch him battle. By 2009 he'd dropped the stage name and kept the notebook.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Kendrick Lamar Duckworth is born in Compton
years.p: His name comes from Temptations singer Eddie Kendricks. He grows up in Section 8 housing and, per Wikipedia, sees a drive-by murder at age five.
years.xp: A seventh-grade English teacher, Regis Inge, connects poetry to hip-hop rhyme schemes and the notebook habit starts. He graduates from Centennial High School in 2005 as a straight-A student.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: K.Dot's first tape, Hub City Threat: Minor of the Year, is mostly freestyles
years.p: Released as K.Dot through Konkrete Jungle Musik, over other people's beats. [[Dave Free|3c4a98dd-7043-420e-8149-79631889ce30]], who drove in from Inglewood to watch him battle, is already in the garage studio.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the tape to 2004 or 2005 and lists it as Youngest Head Nigga in Charge. Free would go on to run the business side of Lamar's career for two decades, including pgLang.

years.src: Wikipedia: Top Dawg Entertainment · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: A computer repair ends in a two-hour audition at TDE
years.p: Dave Free was fixing Anthony "Top Dawg" Tiffith's computer when he played him Lamar's mixtape. Tiffith asked for an audition, and Lamar signed after a two-hour freestyle session.
years.xp:
[[Jay Rock|9880800a-f6f8-4f8f-a00e-b4b664776c0c]] signed first, per the TDE page, and Lamar followed about two weeks later. Lamar bought a minority stake in the label for an undisclosed amount, according to Wikipedia.

Tiffith had founded Top Dawg Entertainment in 2004 as an independent label in Carson, California.

years.big: "One of those situations where I wasn't ready."
q: one of those situations where I wasn't ready
years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Def Jam signs him, then lets him go after he meets Jay-Z
years.p: Lamar's own verdict, per Wikipedia. He got an artist development deal and appeared on two singles by [[The Game|07cc14fb-4784-4a25-804b-2686ed5ef52c]] before Def Jam's president, Jay-Z, let him go.
years.xp: He went back to TDE and the mixtape route.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Hippy
years.h: [[Jay Rock|9880800a-f6f8-4f8f-a00e-b4b664776c0c]], [[ScHoolboy Q|bce6d667-cde8-485e-b078-c0a05adea36d]], [[Ab-Soul|acc12019-10e3-40aa-b4bf-66fbb4a692af]] and Lamar start [[Black Hippy|6fc5c0c6-bf05-4b29-bda0-5fa6cc863785]]
years.p: All four are on TDE, and they start rapping as a unit in South Los Angeles. They never release a group album.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the group as active from 2008 to 2022. TDE president Terrence "Punch" Henderson said the timing for a collective album never worked out, as members kept different schedules.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: K.Dot retires; the Kendrick Lamar EP starts over
years.p: He drops the stage name and swaps freestyles for melancholic original production. Critic Mosi Reeves called it his first standout project, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: It followed the C4 mixtape (January 30, 2009), a tribute to Lil Wayne's Tha Carter III, which Wikipedia says drew criticism. The EP restored his reputation. [[Sounwave|9032140b-c6ba-448d-8f05-5ac16e3aa165]], who has worked with him since this EP, starts a run as chief producer.

eras.title: A debut that sold about 5,000 copies, then Dr. Dre
eras.text: A mixtape sold on iTunes, a debut that moved about 5,000 copies, and then Dr. Dre. It took a year and a half to get from there to a first-week Billboard No. 2.

years.h: Overly Dedicated is the first project he sells at digital retailers
years.p: Released September 14, it peaks at No. 72 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart, per Wikipedia.

q: a powerful document of a tremendously promising young guy figuring out his voice
years.src: Wikipedia: Section.80 · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Section.80 sells about 5,000 copies and debuts at No. 113
years.p: Two characters, Tammy and Keisha, carry a concept record about the crack era and Reagan.
years.xp:
Produced by Sounwave, J. Cole, Terrace Martin and THC. [[ScHoolboy Q|bce6d667-cde8-485e-b078-c0a05adea36d]] and [[Ab-Soul|acc12019-10e3-40aa-b4bf-66fbb4a692af]] appear as guests. Wikipedia says much of it was written in his mother's kitchen and on the tour bus.

Pitchfork gave it 8.0, calling it, per Wikipedia, a powerful document of a promising young guy finding his voice.

years.cap: Lamar and Dr. Dre on stage, April 15, 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar · Wikipedia: Top Dawg Entertainment
years.h: Aftermath and Interscope sign him in a joint venture with TDE
years.p: TDE stays his primary label, and Dr. Dre's Aftermath and Interscope get behind the next record.
years.xp: TDE's deals with Aftermath and Interscope began in 2012, per Wikipedia, and also covered ScHoolboy Q.

years.cap: Lamar at the Pitchfork Music Festival, July 15, 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: Good Kid, M.A.A.D City · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Dr. Dre executive produces good kid, m.A.A.D city
years.p: A concept record about one day in Compton, subtitled "a short film by Kendrick Lamar". It debuts at No. 2 with 242,000 copies and spends over 10 consecutive years on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Producers include [[Pharrell Williams|149f91ef-1287-46da-9a8e-87fee02f1471]], Just Blaze, Hit-Boy and T-Minus. Drake appears on "Poetic Justice", MC Eiht on the title track and Dr. Dre on "Compton", the first song Lamar recorded for it. Wikipedia says [[Lady Gaga|650e7db6-b795-4eb5-a702-5ea2fc46c848]] worked on what became "Bitch, Don't Kill My Vibe" before stepping away over timing and creative differences.

Pitchfork gave it 9.5. Rolling Stone ranked it the greatest concept album of all time in 2022.

eras.title: Eleven names and a Grammy snub
eras.text: One guest verse, one Grammy night that went the wrong way, and a touring stint with Kanye West. By the end of 2014 Lamar was the name everyone else was measuring themselves against.

years.src: Wikipedia: Control (Big Sean song) · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Lamar takes aim at 11 rappers on Big Sean's "Control"
years.p: He names J. Cole, Drake, Meek Mill, [[Big Sean|942a9807-9c1a-4a0e-a285-1fde2c5be9d1]] and [[Jay Electronica|8bf283b9-b1e2-4632-a953-eacd212a543e]] among others, and claims the title of king of New York and the Coast.
years.xp:
The song had been intended for Jay Electronica's album before landing on Big Sean's Hall of Fame, where it was cut over sample clearance, per Wikipedia. Rappers recorded replies; Lamar said the best came from King Los, Joell Ortiz and Joe Budden.

Drake said he didn't really have anything to say about it. Pitchfork ranked it No. 73 on its 2013 songs list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Good Kid, M.A.A.D City · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Zero wins from seven Grammy nominations for good kid, m.A.A.D city
years.p: Macklemore & Ryan Lewis take Best New Artist and Best Rap Album. Macklemore texts Lamar an apology, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Rolling Stone later called it an infamous snub. The nominations included Album of the Year.

eras.title: The difficult record becomes the anthem
eras.text: Jazz, funk, George Clinton and a pile of saxophone. Lamar made his most difficult record just as the country went looking for an anthem, and he supplied one.

years.src: Wikipedia: To Pimp a Butterfly · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: To Pimp a Butterfly lands eight days early
years.p: Scheduled for March 23, it hits iTunes and Spotify on March 15, an error Interscope's CEO called unintentional. It sells 324,000 copies in week one and is his first No. 1.
years.xp:
Recorded between November 2012 and February 2015 with Flying Lotus, Thundercat, Terrace Martin and Dr. Dre as executive producer. [[George Clinton|84683370-5eae-418b-acd8-883ac028a8a0]] appears on "Wesley's Theory", and [[Kamasi Washington|c7a3e868-c6d8-4512-a5ef-f6cbe42899b0]] plays saxophone.

"Mortal Man" closes the record with a 1994 Tupac Shakur interview taken from a Swedish radio host's archive. Pitchfork gave it 9.3 and Metacritic averaged 96.

years.src: Wikipedia: To Pimp a Butterfly · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: "Alright" becomes the chant at protests
years.p: Youth-led marches against police brutality adopt the chorus, and news outlets float it as a modern Black national anthem.
years.xp: Lamar performed it on the BET Awards in 2015, a set Wikipedia describes as controversial. He won Best Male Hip Hop Artist that night.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: untitled unmastered. arrives with dates for titles
years.p: Eight unfinished tracks cut from the To Pimp a Butterfly sessions debut at No. 1 with 178,000 units.
years.xp: Wikipedia says it followed LeBron James asking for access to the untitled songs Lamar had performed on television.

eras.title: A Pulitzer for a rap album
eras.text: Chart records, a Video of the Year, and a Pulitzer Prize for Music, the first given to a work outside classical and jazz. Then a soundtrack for Wakanda.

years.src: Wikipedia: Damn (Kendrick Lamar album) · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: DAMN. opens with 603,000 units and all 14 songs on the Hot 100
years.p: Rihanna and U2 guest. "HUMBLE." gives him his first Hot 100 No. 1 as lead artist.
years.xp:
Lamar said the tracklist could be played in reverse as a full story and that it was premeditated in the studio. A Collectors Edition on December 8, 2017 flips the order.

Pitchfork called it a widescreen masterpiece of rap, per Wikipedia. Producers included Mike Will Made It, DJ Dahi, James Blake, Steve Lacy, BadBadNotGood and The Alchemist.

At the August 2017 MTV VMAs he won five awards, and "HUMBLE." made him the first artist to co-direct a winning Video of the Year, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: He curates and executive produces Black Panther: The Album
years.p: He sings or raps on every track. "All the Stars" earns an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song.

years.cap: Lamar at the Pulitzer Prizes ceremony, May 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Damn (Kendrick Lamar album) · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: DAMN. wins the Pulitzer Prize for Music
years.p: It is the first time the prize goes to a work outside classical and jazz. He also wins Best Rap Album at the Grammys.
years.xp: The DAMN. Tour, which ran July 2017 to July 2018, grossed $62.7 million worldwide, per Wikipedia, his first headline arena run.

eras.title: He builds his own company and leaves TDE
eras.text: Four years between albums, a company with Dave Free, and a double record that opens with him in a therapist's chair. Pitchfork put it at No. 13 on its year-end list.

years.src: Wikipedia: PgLang · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Dave Free and Lamar start pgLang, and say it isn't a label
years.p: "Program language" is the name. Free said it is not a record label, movie studio or publishing house, but something new.
years.xp: Signed acts include [[Baby Keem|81d12ca7-5b89-4d21-8736-860b7400b4eb]] and Tanna Leone. In October 2020 Lamar also signed a worldwide administration deal with Universal Music Publishing Group, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar · Wikipedia: Top Dawg Entertainment
years.h: His next album, a blog post says, will be his last for TDE
years.p: He plans to leave Top Dawg Entertainment after the fifth album and focus on pgLang.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Lamar shares the Super Bowl LVI halftime stage with Dr. Dre's crew
years.p: Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, 50 Cent and Mary J. Blige join him. The show wins a Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Variety Special (Live).

years.src: Wikipedia: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers · Album of the Year: Kendrick Lamar - Mr. Morale & The Big Steppers · BrooklynVegan: Pitchfork's Top 50 Albums of 2022 · Year-End Lists: Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2022
years.h: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers is a double album that goes to therapy
years.p: It opens at No. 1 with 295,000 units, his fourth straight. Pitchfork gave it 7.6 and ranked it No. 13 of 2022.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Stephen Kearse, per Album of the Year, called it ambitious, impressive, and a bit unwieldy. BrooklynVegan noted it did not get Best New Music but still made Pitchfork's year-end list.

Recorded from 2019 to 2022 and executive produced by Lamar as Oklama, with Sounwave, J. Lbs, DJ Dahi and Bekon. Sampha, Beth Gibbons of [[Portishead|8f6bd1e4-fbe1-4f50-aa9b-94c450ec0f11]], Ghostface Killah, Summer Walker and Baby Keem guest, and Eckhart Tolle and Lamar's partner Whitney Alford narrate.

It was his first pgLang release and his last for TDE and Aftermath. Wikipedia reports 295,000 units in week one and 1 billion Spotify streams, a first for a 2022 hip-hop album.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers
years.h: Kodak Black's verse and "Auntie Diaries" draw pushback
years.p: Critics objected to Kodak Black's appearance given his 2016 rape accusation and assault conviction. Others criticized the language on "Auntie Diaries", about his transgender relatives, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Hippy · Wikipedia: Top Dawg Entertainment
years.h: Lamar leaves TDE, and Black Hippy ends with him
years.p: The group never made a record together. Lamar says on GNX that he caused the split, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the group, active from 2008, was ended in effect by his 2022 exit, and that GNX (2024) confirms creative differences with the collective.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Big Steppers Tour · Wikipedia: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers
years.h: He headlines Glastonbury and speaks on reproductive rights
years.p: He makes a political statement in response to the U.S. Supreme Court decision, per Wikipedia. The Big Steppers Tour had opened three days earlier in Milan.
years.xp: The tour ran from June 23, 2022 in Milan to March 23, 2024 in Mexico City, 103 shows, with Baby Keem and Tanna Leone opening. It grossed $110.8 million across 73 tracked shows. The stage resembled a therapist's office.

eras.title: A feud, a reunion and 133.5 million viewers
eras.text: A Grammy for the therapy album, a run of singles that turned a rap feud into a national event, a Los Angeles album, and the biggest halftime audience on record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: Mr. Morale wins Best Rap Album at the 65th Grammys
years.p: "The Heart Part 5" also wins Best Rap Performance and Best Rap Song. He becomes the first artist with Album of the Year nominations for four straight lead albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Not Like Us · Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: "Like That" to "Not Like Us"
years.p: He joins Future and Metro Boomin on "Like That", then answers Drake's "Family Matters" with "Euphoria", "6:16 in LA", "Meet the Grahams" and "Not Like Us" on May 4.
years.xp:
"Not Like Us", produced by Mustard with Sounwave, debuted at No. 1 with 70.9 million streams, per Wikipedia. It arrived less than 20 hours after "Meet the Grahams".

At the 67th Grammys in February 2025 it won all five nominations: Record of the Year, Song of the Year, Best Rap Performance, Best Rap Song and Best Music Video.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Hippy · Wikipedia: Not Like Us
years.h: Black Hippy reunites for seven songs on Juneteenth
years.p: At The Pop Out: Ken & Friends, Jay Rock, ScHoolboy Q, Ab-Soul and Lamar perform together once more. He plays "Not Like Us" five times in a row.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar
years.h: GNX is a record about Los Angeles
years.p: [[SZA|272989c8-5535-492d-a25c-9f58803e027f]] joins him on "Luther", which becomes the longest-charting U.S. No. 1 with 13 non-consecutive weeks, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kendrick Lamar · Wikipedia: Not Like Us
years.h: 133.5 million watch the Super Bowl LIX halftime show
years.p: SZA, Samuel L. Jackson, Serena Williams and Mustard join Lamar in New Orleans. Wikipedia reports it as the most-watched halftime show ever.
